The Galaxy is alive with many forms of life. Some mundane, others beyond common comprehension. This section serves as a guide to introducing different creatures, monsters, and so-called gods to your campaign.

content: **Appearance:** Appears as a woman with tentacles for arms and a smile full of fangs stretching from ear to ear.

**Origin:** Originally a mortal woman who served the Celestial Force entities (the Father, Son, and Daughter). To gain immortality and stop aging, she drank from the Font of Power and bathed in the Pool of Knowledge, which corrupted her into an evil entity representing chaos.

**Powers & Lore:** Trapped in the Maw by the Celestials. She can use Force push, Force lightning, lethal Force energy draining, shapeshifting, mind control, and vision manipulation. She is so dangerous that the Jedi and Sith once had to team up to defeat her.

**Notes:** This monster is not recommended for this era, but is included for the sake of existing in this time period. May be used at GM’s discretion. Abeloth is a campaign-ending threat, essentially a god-like entity. This stat block represents a manifestation or avatar, not her full, unchained power. She should not be fought in conventional combat.
**Life Drain:** 5d toxic damage per second (heals her for damage dealt)
**Force Mind Trick:** (No roll required for mortals, heavy penalties for strong Force users)
**Unkillable 3:** (Cannot be permanently killed without specific Celestial artifacts or combined light/dark rituals)
Vulnerable to combined Light and Dark side attacks.
Trapped in the Maw (Requires significant effort to manifest elsewhere).
Brawling-20, Force Push/Pull-30, Force Lightning-30, Intimidation-25, Psychology-25.

**Origin:** Created long ago, in the days of the old Sith Empire, by Sith Lord Darth Drear using a Force-sensitive, fully self-aware flower called the Murakami Black Orchid. This caused the virus itself to become self-aware and desire to recreate itself.
**Lore:** Sith of the old Empire tried to weaponize it; at least one such effort ended in an accidental outbreak that consumed a warship’s entire crew, leaving the vessel adrift as a plague hulk.

**Symptoms:** Infected individuals die and become highly decomposed, undead hive-minds controlled by the virus. They retain enough intellect to pilot ships and fire blasters. It is transmitted via bites and can only be stopped by destroying the brain or severing the head.
**Notes:** Mindless but capable of basic tool use. Dangerous in swarms.
**ST:** 12 (Slightly stronger than base humanoid due to lack of restraint)
**Undead/Infected:** Immune to stun, shock, fatigue, poison, and disease.
**Injury Tolerance (Unaliving):** Piercing and impaling damage are significantly reduced.
**Infectious Bite:** A successful bite attack requires a HT-4 roll; failure means infection (turns into a zombie in 1d hours).
**Hive Mind:** Can coordinate basic tactics without speaking.
**Brain/Head Targeting:** Takes normal damage only from attacks specifically targeting the head/brain (Targeting penalty -5).
**Fragile (Unnatural):** Total destruction of the body or severing the head instantly destroys it.
**Blaster (if armed):** DX-10 (They retain muscle memory but are inaccurate).
**Appearance:** Large, green-brown reptomammals with massive, muscular jaws, protruding lower tusks, and thick, knobby skin.
**Habitat:** The dense jungle moon of Dxun (orbiting Onderon).
**Behavior:** Highly aggressive pack hunters. They can be incredibly stubborn and are known to charge down prey without hesitation.

**Lore:** Mandalorians stationed on Dxun during the Mandalorian Wars regularly hunted them for sport, food, and to test new recruits. Despite their ferocious nature, some Mandalorians and Onderonian Beast Riders managed to tame them as heavy mounts and beasts of burden.
**Notes:** Ferocious, stubborn pack hunters/heavy mounts on Dxun.
**Tusks (Slam/Charge):** 2d imp (Brawling-14, +2 damage if moving full speed).
**Appearance:** Small, bipedal, reptilian creatures with disproportionately large mouths and a constantly hungry look.
**Behavior:** Voracious scavengers that eat literally anything they can fit in their mouths. They are notoriously bold and will approach camps to steal.

**Lore:** They were an absolute nuisance to Mandalorian forces camped on Dxun because they would eat important mechanical parts, weapon components, and rations. In the KOTOR era, travelers who killed Cannoks often found missing gear and ship components inside their stomachs.
**Universal Digestion:** Can literally eat anything, including metal and plastics.
**Appearance:** Cephalopods that grow up to 30 feet long, possessing seven legs, a mouthful of sharp teeth, and one large eyestalk that pops out of the water.
**Habitat & Diet:** Native to the swamps, sewers, and junkyards of the planet Vodran. They primarily scavenge and hunt smaller prey like fish and crabs.

**Lore:** They are sometimes deliberately introduced into a warship’s or station’s waste-reclamation system to consume organic refuse. They are considered sentient and are sometimes even Force-sensitive.
**Extra Arms (7 Tentacles):** Can grapple multiple targets.
**Constriction Attack:** Automatically does ST damage to grappled foes per turn.
**Chameleon (Water/Trash):** +4 to Stealth in its natural habitat.
**Force Sensitivity:** (Rare variant, usually latent Danger Sense).
**Tentacle Grapple:** DX-12 to hit, initiates grapple.
**Bite:** 1d+1 cut (Brawling-12, usually only on grappled prey).
**Appearance:** Domesticated, dog-like reptavians covered in a mix of scales and plumage. They resemble a smaller cousin of creatures like the Varactyl. Habitat: Taris.
**Behavior:** Docile and friendly, bred specifically as household companions.

**Lore:** Prior to the Mandalorian Wars, these creatures were highly popular pets among the citizens of Taris, especially in the affluent Upper City. Sadly, the species was driven to near-extinction when Darth Malak ordered the orbital bombardment of Taris during the Jedi Civil War.
**Appearance:** Large, glowing, deep-sea aquatic predators. The “Progenitor” is a colossal, ancient variant, easily the size of a capital ship.
**Habitat:** The vast oceans of the planet Manaan.
**Behavior:** Highly aggressive and territorial. Their physiology renders them completely immune to standard blasters, requiring specialized sonic weaponry to subdue or drive them off.

**Lore:** The Progenitor is a colossal, ancient variant worshipped as a deity by the native Selkath of Manaan. It fiercely guards the Hrakert Rift, the planet’s primary source of the miraculous healing fluid, Kolto. Disturbing the Progenitor risks causing a planetary incident, as seen during the Jedi Civil War.
**Notes:** Deadly aquatic predators on Manaan. (For the Progenitor, multiply all physical stats by 10 and give it SM +8, effectively treating it as a hazard/vehicle rather than a creature).
**Immunity to Blasters:** Energy weapons diffuse in the water and have no effect on their physiology.
**Vulnerability (Sonic):** Takes x2 damage from sonic weaponry (e.g., Sonic Emitters).
**Appearance:** Very small, bipedal amphibious reptiles with wide, frog-like mouths and a slightly dopey expression.
**Habitat:** Unknown origins, speculated to possibly be from **Rakata Prime,** but they have spread across the galaxy stowed away on starships.
**Behavior:** Completely harmless, but they have an incredibly rapid reproduction rate. A single Gizka can quickly become an overwhelming swarm.

**Lore:** They are the Star Wars equivalent of a pest infestation (similar to Tribbles). In the KOTOR era, the Ebon Hawk suffered a famous Gizka infestation that required a highly specific, non-lethal poison to convince them to leave the ship.
**Notes:** Pest swarm. Individual stats are meaningless. Treat as a Swarm or Environmental Hazard.
**Effect:** A Gizka infestation ruins food supplies, chews wires (causes random ship malfunctions), and causes immense frustration.

sections.content: **Eradication:** Requires a specific Gizka Poison (Chemistry or Survival roll to synthesize/find) or physically throwing them out the airlock (very tedious). Conventional weapons are useless against the sheer number of them.

content: **Appearance:** Up to 98 feet tall, humanoid, covered in dark fur, and resembles a giant gremlin.
**Habitat:** Lives high in the mountains on the forest moon of Endor.

**Behavior:** Known to come down from the mountains to attack Ewok villages and eat them, which is the primary reason Ewoks build their homes high in the trees and construct large catapults and log traps.
**Appearance:** Large, reptilian, crocodile-like quadrupeds with thick scales and long, powerful tails.
**Habitat:** Planets steeped in Dark Side energy, most notably Korriban and Ambria.

**Behavior:** Amphibious ambush predators. When they bite, they can infect their prey with a dark side poison. Even more dangerously, they possess the innate ability to turn completely invisible by using the Force to mask their presence.

**Lore:** They feed on the dark side of the Force. During the Mandalorian Wars and Jedi Civil War, they flourished on Korriban, feasting on the corpses of fallen Sith and Jedi. If a Force user tapped too deeply into the dark side, it was known to inadvertently summon packs of hungry Hssiss.
**Notes:** Dangerous ambush predator drawn to the Dark Side.
**Dark Side Invisibility:** Can use the Force to become completely invisible (functions as Invisibility advantage, dropping when attacking).
**Dark Side Resonance:** Drawn to large expenditures of FP by Dark Side users.

**Dark Side Venom:** If the bite does damage, target must make a HT-2 roll. Failure results in 1d toxic damage per minute for 5 minutes, and the victim is afflicted with Agony (severe pain penalties) during that time.

**Appearance:** Quadrupedal reptomammals. Standard Kath Hounds are dog-like with thick fur, manes, and small tusks. Horn Kath Hounds are larger, more aggressive variants with prominent horns protruding from their heads.
**Behavior:** Pack hunters. They are usually docile toward humanoids unless provoked, starving, or corrupted by nearby Dark Side artifacts.

**Lore:** Settlers on Dantooine frequently domesticated them as pets and guard dogs. Wild packs were also used by the Jedi Masters at the Dantooine Enclave as a natural training obstacle for young Padawans to test their combat skills and connection to the Force.
**Notes:** Pack hunter of Dantooine. (For Horn Kath Hounds, add +4 ST, +1d impaling horn attack, and DR 2).
**Pack Tactics:** +1 to hit if another Kath Hound is engaged with the same target.
**Appearance:** Terrifying, large, arachnid-like creatures with segmented bodies and four long, spindly legs. They have no visible eyes, relying entirely on smell and ground vibrations to hunt.
**Habitat:** Subterranean caves and dense forests on planets like Dantooine and Kashyyyk.

**Behavior:** Aggressive and territorial swarmers. They spit a highly toxic, paralyzing venom. A hive is always led by a massive Kinrath Matriarch, which is significantly larger, tougher, and produces deadlier toxins.

**Lore:** Kinraths are notoriously difficult to clear out once they establish a hive. Interestingly, the bodies of certain rare Kinrath variants (and Matriarchs) naturally calcify unique crystals that Jedi and Sith frequently harvested to use as focusing crystals in their lightsabers.
**Notes:** Blind, venomous arachnid swarmers. (For Matriarchs, double HP, ST, and make venom HT-6 to resist).
**Vibration Sense:** Detects movement perfectly within 20 yards.
**Spit Venom:** DX-13, Range 5 yards. Hit location doesn’t matter (if unarmored) or must target exposed skin. Target must roll HT-2. Failure means total paralysis for 1d minutes.
**Appearance:** Massive 328-foot-long reptilian predators with 16 legs. Modeled after sauropods.
**Habitat:** The deserts of Tatooine. They swim through the sand and consume rocks to aid digestion.

**Lore:** They can live up to 100 years. Sand People (Tusken Raiders) hunt them as a rite of passage. If a Krayt Dragon ingests a Kyber crystal, it turns into an extremely rare and valuable “Dragon Pearl,” which Jedi sometimes use to create a highly powerful lightsaber with a strange howling sound. Subspecies include the smaller Canyon Krayt and the Greater Krayt.
**Notes:** Massive, legendary beast. Essentially a moving natural disaster.
**Damage Resistance (DR):** 20 (Thick scales and hide, essentially immune to small arms).
**Sand Swimmer:** Can move through loose sand as if it were water.
**Tremorsense:** Detects vibrations in the sand up to 1 mile away.
**Bite/Swallow Whole:** 15d cr (Brawling-12). If it hits a human-sized target, they are swallowed whole (taking 2d acid damage per turn inside).
**Tail Swipe:** 10d cr (Brawling-12, hits an area of 5 yards).

**Appearance:** Large, heavily armored, insectoid predators with a terrifying array of razor-sharp mandibles and multiple scuttling legs. Deadly Laigreks are larger, with a distinct reddish hue to their armor.

**Habitat:** Subterranean caves and abandoned ruins, notably on Dantooine. Behavior: Ambush predators that prefer damp, dark environments. They attack in swarms, using their mandibles to easily slice through armor and flesh.

**Lore:** Following the devastating Sith bombardment of the Jedi Enclave on Dantooine by Darth Malak, hordes of Laigreks migrated from the surrounding caves into the ruins. They infested the sublevels, making it incredibly dangerous for scavengers trying to recover lost Jedi artifacts.
**Notes:** Armored cave insects. (For Deadly Laigreks, add +2 ST, +1 DR).
**Mandible Slice:** 1d+2 cut (Brawling-14). Armor Divisor (2) due to razor sharpness.

**Lore:** The Father, the Son, and the Daughter are three of the most powerful Force entities in existence. They reside in the ethereal realm of Mortis, effectively acting as the anchors for the Force across the entire galaxy. They are not entirely mortal; rather, they are living embodiments of the Force itself.

**Role in the Campaign:** While Mortis is isolated, their influence is absolute. If the fabric of the Force is catastrophically threatened (such as the release of Abeloth, massive breaches in the Maw, or apocalyptic superweapons targeting the cosmic balance), they can and will project themselves into the physical galaxy. Their goal is always balance. They will assist players to seal an apocalyptic threat but may turn their unimaginable power against the players immediately afterward if the players are deemed responsible for the imbalance.
**Appearance:** An incredibly old, tall humanoid with flowing white robes and a stern, sad demeanor.
**Powers:** He possesses absolute authority over both the Light and Dark sides. His mere presence suppresses Force usage around him. He cannot be fought conventionally.
**ST/DX/HT:** N/A (Treat as untouchable by conventional means).

**Traits:** Absolute Force Nullification (Anyone within 100 yards must win a Quick Contest of Will against his 40 to use any Force power). Cosmic Telekinesis (Can halt moving starships or redirect superweapon blasts with a gesture).

**Vulnerability (The Dagger of Mortis):** The Father is immortal and completely immune to all physical, energy, and Force attacks, with one singular exception. The Dagger of Mortis, an ancient, mystical relic kept hidden on Mortis, can bypass all of his cosmic defenses. A successful strike with the Dagger is the only way to permanently kill him (or his children).

sections.content: 2. The Son (Embodiment of the Dark Side)

content: **Appearance:** A pale, bald humanoid cloaked in dark, shadowy robes. He can shapeshift into a massive, terrifying gargoyle/bat creature.
**Powers:** He represents ambition, passion, and the destructive nature of the Dark Side. His power is overwhelming, capable of corrupting individuals simply by speaking to them.

**Traits:** Shapeshifting (Gargoyle form grants Flight 20 and DR 15). Cosmic Lightning (15d energy, Armor Divisor 10, cannot be absorbed by lightsabers without a critical success). Aura of Corruption (Proximity causes FP drain to Light Side users).

sections.content: 3. The Daughter (Embodiment of the Light Side)

content: **Appearance:** A glowing, ethereal woman with bright, luminescent hair and elegant robes. She can shapeshift into a massive, majestic Griffin-like creature.
**Powers:** She represents compassion, healing, and the protective nature of the Light Side. She acts as a shield against the Son’s destructive tendencies.

**Traits:** Shapeshifting (Griffin form grants Flight 25 and DR 10). Cosmic Healing (Can completely restore HP/FP of allies in an instant, even bringing the recently deceased back to life). Aegis Barrier (Projected Force barrier with 100 DR, absorbing all incoming damage in a massive radius).
**Appearance:** Enormous dragon-like creatures with scaly, lizard-like skin and two large tusks curving inward to fight competitors. Some accounts claim they were the size of a small city.

**Lore:** Native to Mandalore, where they made their lairs in giant underground Beskar mines near the Living Waters. Mandalore the Great was the first to fight, tame, and ride one. The very first Mandalorian mask was carved from a Mythosaur’s highly impenetrable sternum bone. They served as the symbol of the Mandalorian people but were driven to near extinction by young warriors hunting them as a rite of passage.
**Notes:** Near-mythical titans of Mandalore. These stats represent a “small” specimen.
**Damage Resistance (DR):** 25 (Bone plating, highly resistant to energy and physical trauma).
**Appearance:** Horrifying, hunched, zombie-like humanoids with pale, rotting skin, elongated limbs, and razor-sharp claws and teeth.
**Behavior:** Mindless, ravenous pack hunters driven only by the instinct to feed and spread their infection. They move with unnatural speed and aggression.

**Lore:** Not a natural species, but the result of a Sith biological plague engineered by the ancient Sith Lord Karness Muur. A simple scratch or bite from a Rakghoul transmits the disease, rapidly mutating the victim into a Rakghoul within hours. They were the primary terror of the Tarisian Outcasts during the KOTOR era.

**Infectious Claws/Bite (Rakghoul Plague):** Any physical damage dealt by a Rakghoul requires the victim to roll HT-4. Failure means infection. The victim mutates into a Rakghoul in 1d hours unless treated with a specific, rare serum. Jedi/Sith have advantage on this roll due to the Force.

**Appearance:** Mammal/reptile carnivores standing roughly 16.5 feet tall with long arms. Origin & Behavior: Native to Dathomir. Despite their dangerous appearance, they are naturally gentle, social, and can form deep bonds with their handlers -- a beast-keeper has been known to grieve openly when a captive rancor is slain in some crime lord’s arena pit. Over time, they are often provoked into violence to be used as fighters or mounts.
**Subspecies:** Jungle Rancor (found on Felucia and Teth), Rage Rancor (taller, meaner, with horns), and the Rancor Dragon (mutated by Sith magic to have wings and fly).
**Damage Resistance (DR):** 8 (Thick hide, deflects standard blaster fire easily).

sections.content: **Grapple:** DX-13 to grab. Can squeeze for ST damage (4d) per turn.

content: **Appearance:** A giant flesh pit reaching up to 330 feet deep with roots to suck up nutrients and tentacles to sting and paralyze prey.

**Behavior:** Purposely keeps prey alive for eons to digest them over time because it can go a long time between meals. It separates sentient from non-sentient creatures, keeping the minds of sentient beings processing even as their bodies dissolve, eventually merging their consciousnesses into a giant hive mind.
**Digestive Acid:** 1d acid damage per minute once swallowed.
**Tentacle Grab:** DX-10, pulls target toward the maw (opposed ST check).
**Paralyzing Sting:** If grabbed, target must roll HT-3 or be paralyzed for hours.
**Appearance:** Large, eyeless, bat-like avians with leathery wings and sharp fangs.
**Habitat:** The deep, dark caves and tombs of Korriban.
**Behavior:** Highly aggressive and fiercely territorial. They rely entirely on echolocation and attack in massive swarms, overwhelming intruders.

**Lore:** They are considered pests by the Sith, roosting in the ancient tombs of the Dark Lords. While a single Shyrack is easily dealt with, their tendency to swarm makes them incredibly dangerous even to trained Sith Acolytes attempting to pass their trials.
**Notes:** Bat-like pests of Korriban. Dangerous in swarms.
**Sonar/Echolocation:** Maps surroundings perfectly in the dark.
**Appearance:** Up to half a mile long, housing entire ecosystems inside of them.

**Movement & Hunting:** Features telescope-like eyes that constantly detect starlight. If the light is blocked, it jumps off its asteroid and flies through space until it finds another. It burrows deep into asteroids, spreading root-like structures to absorb nutrients, and lunges out to eat passing ships, creatures, or other asteroids.
**Reproduction:** Reproduces through fission, creating immediate, independent clones.
**Lore:** Evil scientists once tried to weaponize them by growing them to massive sizes and strapping hyperdrives to them so they could consume entire star systems.
**Notes:** Environmental hazard. Encounters usually involve flying ships into or away from it, not fighting it with hand-weapons.
**Lunge/Swallow:** Uses Piloting (or DX) to dodge the lunge. If hit, the ship is swallowed into the cavernous digestive tract.
**Appearance:** Ancient, dead-looking humanoids with claws that can rip through opponents. Anyone who looks at them sees their own decaying face.
**Powers:** Extremely strong with the Force, utilizing powers like life drain, Force grip, Force sight, and Force lightning. They scream in the vacuum of space like banshees.

**Behavior:** Nearly invincible to conventional weapons like blasters. They specifically hunt Force users, especially Jedi. They are theorized to be constructed purely out of Dark Side energy and frequently traumatized deep space sailors.
**Notes:** Terrifying space demons targeting Force users.
**Injury Tolerance (Insubstantial/Energy):** Highly resistant to physical and energy weapons (half damage from blasters/slugthrowers). Lightsabers do full damage.
**Telepathy (Scream):** Emits a horrifying psychic scream. Target must make a Will-4 check or be stunned for 1d turns.
**Force Powers:** Force Crush-15, Force Lightning-15 (4d energy).
**Appearance:** Massive, hulking, simian-like monstrosities with bony protrusions, pale skin, and immense, muscular arms. Greater Storm Beasts are even larger, radiating dark side energy.
**Habitat:** The ruined surface of Malachor V (Available between **3960-3951 BBY)**.
**Behavior:** Viciously aggressive. They rely on brute physical strength to pummel enemies and can unleash devastating sonic roars that crush internal organs.

**Lore:** They were once normal creatures native to Malachor V. When the Mandalorian Wars ended with the activation of the catastrophic Mass Shadow Generator weapon, the planet was shattered. The surviving creatures were horrifically mutated by the gravitational anomalies and the intense Dark Side energies of the planet, turning them into mindless engines of destruction.
**Notes:** Malachor V mutants. (Greater Storm Beasts: +10 ST, +2 DR, Force Resistance).
**Dark Side Taint:** Heals rapidly (Regeneration: 1 HP/min) while on Malachor V or strong Dark Side nexuses.

sections.content: **Sonic Roar:** Every 3 turns, can emit a roar. Area effect (Cone, 10 yards). 3d cr damage (internal/sonic, bypasses most non-sealed armor).

content: **Appearance:** Massive space tentacle monsters reaching over 24,000 feet (4.5 miles) in size. They feature multiple eyes and electrified tentacles used to trap prey.
**Habitat:** Found living in outer space, specifically around the planet Kessel and the dangerous Maw vortex.

**Lore:** A smuggler is said to have woken one while running spice past Kessel, luring it into the Maw to shake pursuit. In a separate tale, a Sith Lord fought one, endured the Force-visions it hurled at him, subdued it with the dark side, and rode it across the stars -- until his master reached out through the Force and made the creature crush itself.
**Notes:** Epic space encounter. Treat as a capital ship or environmental hazard in space combat.
**Tentacles:** Do starship-scale damage and can grapple freighters.
**Electrified Grasp:** Deals continuous ion/energy damage to grappled ships.
**Mind Bending (Force Vision):** Any sentient being near the creature must make a Will-6 roll or suffer intense, paralyzing hallucinations and visions of their death.
**Appearance:** Small, harmless, monkey-like primates with flat faces, large eyes, and leathery skin.
**Habitat:** The dense canopy and dangerous Shadowlands of Kashyyyk. Behavior: Skittish tree-dwellers that spend their time foraging for grubs and fruits.

**Lore:** During the KOTOR era, the Czerka Corporation heavily poached the Tach. They discovered that a gland in the Tach’s brain produced a fluid that, when processed, became a highly addictive stimulant and a primary ingredient in the famous “Tarisian Ale.”
**Skittish:** Runs away at the first sign of danger.
**Appearance:** Massive, hulking, tusked monstrosities resembling a cross between a rancor and a demon. They have thick, leathery hides covered in vicious spikes.
**Habitat:** Dark Side nexus planets (Korriban, the Shadowlands of Kashyyyk, and deep caves on Tatooine).
**Behavior:** Solitary, incredibly dangerous apex predators. They specifically hunt Force sensitives, drawn to their power like blood in the water.

**Lore:** Terentateks are not natural creatures; they are abominations created by ancient Sith alchemy. Their hides are naturally highly resistant to both Force powers and lightsaber strikes. They became such a massive threat that the Jedi Order initiated a galaxy-wide “Great Hunt” a few decades before the Mandalorian Wars to drive them to extinction, though several powerful specimens survived.
**Force Immunity/Resistance:** Cannot be directly affected by Force Push, Pull, Lightning, or Mind Control.
**Lightsaber Resistance:** DR 10 against Lightsabers. (DR 5 against blasters/physical attacks).
**Force Tracker:** Can sense Force sensitives within a 10-mile radius.

sections.content: **Venomous Quills:** If grappled or in close combat, attackers take 1d pi damage.

content: **Appearance:** Large, quadrupedal beasts with canine and feline traits, glowing red eyes, prominent horns on their heads, and a barbed tail.
**Behavior:** Fearless, highly intelligent pack hunters. They are fiercely loyal to the Sith and can communicate with one another using unknown languages.

**Lore:** Mutated through Sith alchemy, they were specifically engineered to guard the tombs of the ancient Dark Lords of the Sith. They are incredibly patient and are rumored to be able to enter a state of hibernation for centuries, awakening only when a tomb robber or unworthy intruder enters their domain.
**Suspended Animation:** Can sleep for centuries without food/water.
**Pack Tactics:** Highly coordinated, will attempt to flank and trip opponents.
**Appearance:** Carnivorous apex predators just under 10 feet tall with white fur that acts as incredible camouflage. Based on the mythological Yeti.

**Behavior:** Hunts on four legs. Instead of killing immediately, they rush and stun their prey to keep the meat fresh. They take victims back to their caves and use their hot breath and saliva to freeze/stick them to the ceiling for later consumption. Their main food source is Tauntauns, though they will eat humans.
**Claw Smash:** 2d+1 cr (Brawling-13). Will frequently target the head/torso to stun prey.
**Appearance:** Enormous, incredibly heavily armored reptilian beasts resembling a spiked, predatory dinosaur.
**Behavior:** Solitary apex predators. They are extremely territorial, highly aggressive, and fear absolutely nothing.

**Lore:** The Zakkeg is considered the ultimate hunting trophy by the Mandalorian Neo-Crusaders. Its hide is nearly impenetrable, capable of deflecting high-powered blaster bolts and even resisting lightsaber strikes. Taking down a Zakkeg is a rite of passage that elevates a Mandalorian warrior to legendary status among their clan.
**Impenetrable Hide (DR):** 15 (Resists blasters heavily, partially resists lightsabers).
**Spiked Armor:** Anyone attacking it unarmed or grappling it takes 1d imp damage.
**Appearance:** Over 300 feet tall, resembling a giant snake-reptile with three arms, a massive spiked tail, and heavily plated armor.
**Durability:** Its armor is invulnerable to explosions, blaster fire, and even lightsabers.

**Lore:** Long thought extinct, one was rediscovered when a mining blast opened a deep sinkhole. Another was worshipped as a god by a wild-space cult until it was slain. A captured specimen brought to Coruscant broke its bonds and rampaged through the city before it was finally put down with poison gas -- and Sith alchemists are rumored to have recovered its tissue, hoping to clone the beast as a weapon.
**Notes:** A kaiju-level threat. Requires heavy artillery or very specific environmental hazards to defeat.
**Invulnerable Armor (DR):** 100+ (Cosmic: Deflects lightsabers, ignores conventional bombs and turbolasers).
**Extra Arm (3rd Arm):** Can grapple or smash while moving.
**Vulnerability:** Weak to specific toxic gases (which bypass its armor entirely).

sections.content: The galaxy during the Mandalorian Wars is a fractured, bleeding place. The Republic’s borders are constantly shifting under the relentless pressure of the Mandalorian crusade, while corporations like Czerka exploit the chaos in the Rim. To understand the strategic and political realities of this era, one must understand the worlds that serve as its battlegrounds, sanctuaries, and graveyards.

A Note on Galactic Timelines: This era (spanning roughly 3964 BBY to 3951 BBY) is a period of great, and often catastrophic change. Some worlds described below will not survive the coming decade intact. For worlds that undergo drastic transformations due to the war or the subsequent Jedi Civil War, a timeline of changes has been provided.
For a visual representation of these hyperlane routes, territorial borders, and strategic chokepoints, please refer to the accompanying galaxy map.

The heart of the Galactic Republic, representing civilization, wealth, and overwhelming bureaucracy. While largely insulated from the front lines of the Mandalorian Wars, the political decisions made here dictate the fate of billions.

content: **Description:** The ecumenopolis (city-planet) capital of the Galactic Republic and the home of the Jedi High Council. While its glittering upper levels are steeped in wealth and political maneuvering, its dark, labyrinthine underlevels are a haven for criminals and smugglers. During the war, Coruscant is a place of weariness, where politicians argue over troop deployments and Jedi Masters debate the morality of intervention.
**Languages:** Basic (native to nearly the entire population; the origin point of Basic as the galaxy’s lingua franca).

**Notable Resources:** None native. The ecumenopolis mines nothing and grows nothing; it is the galaxy's great refinery and fabrication floor, importing raw stock from a thousand worlds and turning out finished goods -- manufactured components, Clari-crystalline optics and Data-Crystals (Ch10), starship parts, and above all information. What Coruscant produces is industry, credit, and political leverage.
**Notable Locations:** The Jedi Temple, The Senate Rotunda, The Underworld (Level 1313 & Below).

**Description:** A peaceful, mountainous world famous for its art, culture, and philosophy. Alderaan remains a staunch supporter of the Republic war effort, though its pacifistic ideals are severely tested by the brutal realities of the Mandalorian crusade.

**Notable Resources:** None of note. A temperate world of grasslands and mountains, Alderaan trades in foodstuffs, fine art, and craftsmanship rather than extraction; its wealth is cultural and agricultural, and its heavy materials are imported -- a deliberate reflection of its pacifist leanings.
**Notable Locations:** Aldera Royal Palace, University of Alderaan.

sections.content: Worlds closer to the Core that serve as vital industrial hubs, trade centers, and staging grounds for the Republic Military.

content: **Description:** A harsh, jungle world with a heavily fortified capital city, Iziz. Onderon is a key strategic world and one of the earliest targets of the Mandalorian Neo-Crusaders. Its moon, Dxun, is a savage, beast-infested jungle where Mandalore the Indomitable was once defeated, and where the Mandalorians have established heavily fortified camps.
**Languages:** Basic (Onderon); Dxun has no settled population of its own.

**Notable Resources:** Jungle produce and beast-derived materials rather than ore. Onderon farms behind its walls; its moon Dxun is a savage wildland whose predators (Ch19's Boma and kin) yield tough hides and trophy components, and whose canopy gives dense jungle timber (Standard- to Brylark-grade wood, Ch10/Ch12). No metal industry of note -- durable goods come up from the Republic.
**Notable Locations:** The Walled City of Iziz (Onderon), Mandalorian Forward Camp (Dxun), Tomb of Freedon Nadd (Dxun).

**Description:** An aquatic planet populated by the neutral Selkath. Manaan’s strict neutrality is respected only because it is the galaxy’s sole source of kolto, a miraculous healing fluid essential to both the Republic and Mandalorian war machines.
**Languages:** Selkath (native to the Selkath, who often speak Basic only Accented or not at all -- see Chapter 3); Basic (spoken by Republic and offworld visitors, and some Selkath officials).

**Notable Resources:** Kolto -- the flagship. Manaan is the galaxy's sole natural source of the raw medical material behind every Medpac and kolto tank (Ch1/Ch10), drawn from the ocean depths under fierce Selkath control. The war's entire medical supply runs through Ahto City, and Republic and Sith alike pay wartime premiums to keep the taps open -- the neutrality that guards the monopoly is the planet's real strategic weight. Beyond kolto the oceans give food and desalinated water but little metal; Manaan imports its durable goods.
**Notable Locations:** Ahto City, Hrakert Station, The Selkath High Court.

sections.content: The resource-rich borders where the Republic’s military is stretched to its breaking point. These worlds often bear the brunt of the Mandalorian scorched-earth tactics.

content: **Description:** Homeworld of the feline Cathar species. The planet remains a scarred, tragic reminder of Mandalorian brutality, motivating many rogue Jedi to join the war effort.
**Languages:** Catharese (native, though scattered and diminished since the Genocide); Basic (spoken by most Cathar integrated into Republic space).

**Notable Resources:** Depleted. Before the Genocide, Cathar's colossal tree-cities were a source of prized structural timber and the craft-goods of a thriving culture; the Mandalorian burning left scorched plains and ruins, and what little the survivors recover is scavenged Scrap Metal (Ch10/Ch13) from the wreckage rather than harvested stock. A resource world turned graveyard.
**Pre-3973 BBY:** A thriving, ecologically balanced world dominated by massive tree-cities and plains.
**3973 BBY:** The Genocide of Cathar. Cassus Fett leads the Mandalorians in exterminating the population, burning the tree-cities and driving the survivors into the ocean to be slaughtered.
**Notable Locations:** The Ruined Tree-Cities, The Memorial.
**Description:** A massive forest world populated by the Wookiees. Heavily exploited by the Czerka Corporation, which has set up lucrative and deeply unethical slaving and logging operations.
**Languages:** Shyriiwook (native to the Wookiees, who can learn to understand Basic but cannot physically speak it -- see Chapter 3).

**Notable Resources:** Wroshyr Wood -- the flagship. The great wroshyr trees give a heavy, uncommonly strong timber (Ch11/Ch12: 40 CR/lb; the traditional stock of Bowcasters, and prized for lightsaber hilts and melee hafts). Czerka Corporation strips it under brutal logging concessions worked by Wookiee slave labour, and the deadly Shadowlands floor yields exotic saps and beast materials besides.
**Notable Locations:** Rwookrrorro, Czerka Outpost, The Shadowlands.

**Description:** A devastated Mid Rim world. To send a message to the Republic, the Mandalorians wiped out the Republic forces and the native civilian population (the Stereb) in a single brutal strike.
**Languages:** Basic (the human population); the native Stereb’s own tongue, now largely lost alongside the world itself.

**Notable Resources:** None. The Mandalorian nuclear bombardment glassed the surface and sterilized the biosphere; the Stereb cities and human settlements are slag. Nothing is harvested here now -- Serroco is a poisoned monument, not a supply world.
**Pre-3963 BBY:** A peaceful world with a mixture of Stereb cities and human settlements, transformed into a Republic Navy staging ground.
**3963 BBY:** The Battle of Serroco. The Mandalorians bombard the planet with nuclear missiles. The surface is glassed, sterilizing the biosphere and forcing the few survivors deep underground.

sections.content: The fringes of civilized space. The Outer Rim is lawless, dangerous, and heavily contested. It is here that the Mandalorian Wars are fought most fiercely, and where ancient, dark secrets lie buried.

content: **Description:** An ecumenopolis marked by extreme class segregation. Taris is a major strategic hub on the Outer Rim, making it a highly contested prize and a hotbed for swoop gangs and mercenaries.
**Languages:** Basic (the dominant tongue at every level of the city); Huttese (widely spoken in the Lower City and Undercity, where Exchange and Hutt-affiliated interests hold real power).

**Notable Resources:** Salvage and manufacture. The upper tiers turn out manufactured goods and refined components, while the Undercity is a vast field of Scrap Metal (Ch10/Ch13: 10 CR/lb) picked over by scavengers and swoop gangs -- the cheapest crafting stock in the sector, at the cost of its Rakghoul-infested depths. After 3956 BBY the whole world becomes the galaxy's largest scrapyard.
**3964 - 3959 BBY:** A bustling, corrupt metropolis. The wealthy live in the gleaming Upper City, while the poor and mutated Rakghouls rot in the Undercity.

**3956 BBY:** The Destruction of Taris. Darth Malak’s Sith fleet subjects the planet to a devastating orbital bombardment, reducing the towering spires to rubble and ash to prevent the escape of Jedi Bastila Shan.
**Notable Locations (Pre-3956 BBY):** The Upper City, The Lower City, The Undercity.
**Description:** An idyllic, sparsely populated world of rolling plains and grasslands, home to a secluded Jedi Enclave.

**Notable Resources:** Lightsaber crystals -- the flagship. The Crystal Caves beneath the plains grow natural focusing crystals (Ch12's Primary Focusing / Kyber table), a quiet pilgrimage for Jedi cutting their first blades. Above ground the world is pastoral -- grain, kath-hound hides, little else -- which is exactly why the Order hid an Enclave here. Malak's bombardment scatters the Jedi, but the caves endure.
**3964 - 3959 BBY:** A serene sanctuary. The Enclave serves as a training ground for Padawans and a place of tense ideological debate regarding the Mandalorian Wars.

**3956 BBY:** Darth Malak discovers the hidden Enclave and launches a Sith bombardment, destroying the academy and killing or scattering the Jedi. The ruins are subsequently overrun by mercenaries and scavengers.
**Notable Locations:** The Jedi Enclave, The Crystal Caves, Ancient Ruins.
**Description:** Once an important Republic agricultural and administrative world on the Outer Rim, its fate serves as the tragic opening note to the Jedi Civil War.

**Notable Resources:** Agricultural, then reconstructive. Once a lush agriworld and tourist beacon, Telos grew food and hospitality rather than materials; after the bombardment it produces nothing until the great Restoration Project, whose materiel is imported and staged from Citadel Station. A world defined by what is shipped in, not dug out.
**Pre-3959 BBY:** A lush, vibrant agriworld and popular tourist destination, serving as a shining beacon of the Republic in the Outer Rim.

**3959 BBY:** Marking the beginning of the Jedi Civil War, Admiral Saul Karath (under the orders of Darth Revan) launches an orbital bombardment, scorching the planet’s biosphere and rendering the surface completely barren.
**3951 BBY:** A massive Republic restoration project is underway. Citadel Station orbits the planet, overseeing heavily shielded “Restoration Zones” on the blasted surface below.
**Notable Locations (3951 BBY Era):** Citadel Station, Restoration Zones.

**Description:** A fractured planet whose exposed core is mined for highly volatile, weapons-grade fuel. It serves as a crucial, remote supply point for the Republic and the Telos restoration project.

**Notable Resources:** Volatile mining fuel. Peragus's fractured core is stripped for highly volatile, weapons-grade fuel (a refined combustible in the Ch10 consumable-fuel family) and staged for passing ships -- a crucial, deadly remote depot. The same volatility that makes the fuel valuable destroys the colony in 3951 BBY. The mining is the world; there is nothing else.
**Pre-3951 BBY:** A functioning, albeit extremely hazardous, orbital mining facility extracting raw fuel from the planet’s fractured asteroid field.

**3951 BBY:** The Destruction of Peragus. Following the arrival of the Jedi Exile and a pursuing Sith strike team, the volatile asteroid field ignites. The resulting explosion obliterates the facility and the surrounding asteroids, crippling the Republic’s fuel supply in the sector.
**Notable Locations:** Peragus Mining Facility, The Fuel Depot, The Administration Level.

**Description:** Yavin is a massive, crimson gas giant. While the planet itself is uninhabitable, its orbital space houses a solitary supply depot. Its jungle moon, Yavin 4, remains haunted by the dark legacy of the Great Sith War.
**Languages:** Basic; the ancient Massassi/Sith ruins on Yavin 4 carry inscriptions in the ancient Sith language (see Chapter 3), though no living population speaks it there.

**Notable Resources:** Tibanna and Corusca gems -- from the gas giant. Yavin's atmosphere is a natural well of Tibanna Gas (Ch10/Ch11: 75 CR/lb, the working fluid of every blaster pack), and its crushing depths grow Corusca Gems (Ch12: a 20,000 CR secondary power crystal). The jungle moon Yavin 4 is a trove of a darker kind -- the Massassi temples and Exar Kun's tomb hold ancient Sith artifacts and dark-side-attuned relics for those reckless enough to take them (Ch8/Ch12). Suvam Tan's orbital station trades experimental gear until Trandoshan raiders end it in 3956 BBY.
**3996 BBY (Pre-Mandalorian Wars):** The defeat of the Sith Lord Exar Kun on Yavin 4. His spirit is bound to the Massassi temples, and the moon is subsequently quarantined and shunned by the Jedi.
**3964 - 3956 BBY:** The Rodian inventor Suvam Tan operates Yavin Station in orbit around the gas giant, providing high-end, experimental gear to those brave (or wealthy) enough to find it.
**3956 BBY:** Yavin Station is raided by Trandoshan mercenaries and subsequently abandoned by Suvam Tan.
**Notable Locations:** Yavin Station (Orbit), Massassi Temples (Yavin 4), Exar Kun’s Tomb (Yavin 4).

**Description:** The cultural heart and homeworld of the Mandalorian clans. It is a harsh, rugged world that breeds hardened warriors. From here, Mandalore the Ultimate orchestrates his galaxy-spanning crusade.
**Languages:** Mando’a (native to Mandalorians, alongside Basic for most who deal with the wider galaxy -- see Chapter 3).

**Notable Resources:** Beskar -- the flagship. The Beskar Mines yield Mandalorian iron (Ch10/Ch11/Ch13: 1,500 CR/lb, x2.0 DR, +5 DR vs energy -- the hardest armour stock in the book), the metal of Mandalorian beskar'gam. It is clan-guarded and rarely sold offworld, and the smithing that works it, Metallurgy (Beskar), is taught only within the clans (Ch3). Mandalore is otherwise a harsh, rugged world whose truest export is warriors.
**Description:** A desolate, red-rock planet steeped in the Dark Side of the Force. It is the ancient graveyard of the Sith Lords.
**Languages:** the ancient Sith language (the historical Sith Empire’s ceremonial tongue, preserved in tombs and holocrons -- see Chapter 3); Basic (spoken by modern visitors, scholars, and looters).

**Notable Resources:** Sith relics, not raw stock. The Valley of the Dark Lords is a graveyard of tombs, holocrons, and dark-side artifacts (Ch8, Ch19), and the desolate world is where a Dark Side adept bleeds and attunes a synthetic crystal -- the Ch12 Synthetic (Red) Kyber, forged through Dark Side meditation -- and gathers the materials of Sith Alchemy (Ch8). Nothing is farmed or mined here in the ordinary sense; what Korriban offers is power, and the ruin it costs.
**3964 - 3960 BBY:** Largely abandoned and forbidden, left to tomb robbers and the ghosts of ancient Sith.
**3959 - 3956 BBY:** Reclaimed by Darth Revan’s Sith Empire. A massive Sith Academy operates openly, training dark side acolytes through lethal trials.
**Notable Locations:** Valley of the Dark Lords, Dreshdae, The Sith Academy.
**Description:** A jagged world shrouded in dark energy. It is a place of ultimate taboo for the Mandalorians, and the site of the most horrific tragedy of the era.
**Languages:** none -- a dead world with no living population since the Mass Shadow Generator.

**Notable Resources:** None -- a shattered world. The Mass Shadow Generator crushed Malachor's surface and, in 3951 BBY, the planet itself; the buried Trayus Academy is a Force wound rather than a resource. Whatever the ancient Sith left lies lost under debris and dark-side dread. Nothing is harvested from a corpse world.
**Pre-3960 BBY:** A forbidden, jagged, and dangerous world, home to the buried ancient Sith Trayus Academy, but structurally whole.

**3960 BBY:** The Battle of Malachor V. Jedi General Meetra Surik (The Exile) orders the activation of the Mass Shadow Generator. The superweapon crushes the Mandalorian and Republic fleets, pulling them into the planet. The world’s crust fractures, leaving a cracked, jagged hellscape wracked by violent lightning and gravity anomalies.
**3951 BBY:** The complete destruction of Malachor V. The Mass Shadow Generator is reactivated by the Exile, destroying the planet entirely and reducing it to a drifting asteroid field.
**Notable Locations (3960-3951 BBY):** Trayus Academy, The Stormscape.

sections.content: The frontier immediately beyond the Outer Rim Territories. Systems here are sparsely mapped, poorly understood, and entirely beyond the reach of Republic law. It is a haven for explorers, exiles, and those fleeing the devastation of the Mandalorian advance.

content: **Description:** A harsh, frozen world characterized by its bitter cold and violent ice storms. Completely insignificant strategically to the Republic, it serves as a perfect hiding place or staging ground for Mandalorian splinter groups looking to disappear.
**Languages:** Basic (what little population exists is offworld military/scientific personnel; no native sapient species calls the ice home).

**Notable Resources:** Nothing native. A frozen, storm-lashed waste with no industry and no settled population beyond offworld personnel; its only caches are hidden Mandalorian arms in the Twin Ice Canyons -- and, in clan legend, a buried relic that once pointed the Mandalorians toward the Sith. A place to hide things, not to mine them.
**Notable Locations:** The Twin Ice Canyons, Hidden Mandalorian Caches.

sections.content: A vast, unmapped expanse of the galaxy separated from the Republic by a tangled web of hyperspace anomalies, solar storms, and gravitational hazards. Navigating this region is near-suicide without specialized data or Force sensitivity. It is a place of ancient myths, forgotten empires, and looming threats.

content: **Description:** A tropical, oceanic world that is the forgotten homeworld of the Infinite Empire. It is deliberately shrouded from the galaxy by a deadly disruptor field that violently forces incoming starships to crash.

**Languages:** Rakatan (the ancient, now largely extinct tongue of the Rakata Empire that built the Star Forge -- see Chapter 3); understood by few outside dedicated scholars and the last scattered Rakata.

**Notable Resources:** Ancient Rakatan relic-technology. Lehon is an archaeological trove rather than a materials world: the ruins of the Infinite Empire and the dark-side-powered Star Forge in orbit are priceless, dangerous ancient technology far beyond present manufacture (see Ch21's lore). What the Rakata built cannot be sourced -- only recovered, and rarely survived. Beyond the relics, tropical ocean and jungle with scattered Rakatan island settlements.

**3959 - 3956 BBY:** Serves as the hidden capital of Darth Revan and Malak’s Sith Empire. The massive, dark-side-powered space station known as the Star Forge orbits its star, churning out an endless fleet of warships.
**3956 BBY:** The Battle of Rakata Prime. The Republic fleet destroys the Star Forge, and the planet is subsequently left alone, descending back into obscurity.
**Notable Locations:** Temple of the Ancients, The Star Forge (Orbit), Rakatan Island Settlements.

**Description:** A dark, storm-drenched jungle world constantly crackling with dark side energy. Officially, it does not exist on any Republic star chart. Unofficially, it is the secret rallying point for the “True” Sith Empire that survived the Great Hyperspace War centuries ago, lying in wait to strike back at the Republic.

**Languages:** unknown to the wider galaxy -- the true Sith Empire’s living language (see Chapter 3’s note on Sith, Imperial) remains a secret of the true Sith Emperor’s hidden domain during this era.

**Notable Resources:** Unknown. The hidden Sith Empire's storm-wracked capital appears on no Republic chart, and its industry, materiel, and resources are a secret of the Empire (see Ch21's timeline). Nothing here reaches the galactic market -- and a character who learns what Dromund Kaas produces has stumbled onto something the Empire will kill to keep buried.
**Notable Locations:** Kaas City, The Dark Temple (Under Construction), Sith Citadel.
